name: audio1010_hud_prompt
prompt: Edit the supplied Bullets of Fury arcade HUD reference into a new text-free shipping HUD housing. Preserve its richly shaded Neo Geo pixel-art dark steel, chrome rivets and bright amber status-light aesthetic. Redesign layout for an EXTRA WIDE shallow bottom HUD, 7:1 visible artwork width-to-height, whole width complete from left to right, no clipped edges. The two prominent angled trapezoidal counter tabs MUST stick UP above the main frame: one wide empty tab at far upper left for lives, and one wide empty tab at far upper right for missiles. Below the tabs only FOUR large adjacent empty main panels: left 22% two empty horizontal meter wells stacked vertically (roll/somersault); next 14% one large empty weapon icon recess; center 40% large title recess, thick empty long special meter well, and two small stat recesses below; right 24% one large empty targeting/lock recess. Remove the radar entirely from this bottom HUD. Every well has very dark flat navy black interiors. NO text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO icons, NO radar picture, NO filled colored meters. Thin chrome borders and vivid amber indicator bulbs, generous usable recesses, intricate authored pixel shading, crisp sharp pixel edges. One complete horizontal housing only, centered on a fully transparent canvas, tightly contained in shallow panorama with small transparent padding. Do not draw any game scene or mockup. The TOP angled lives/missile tabs must remain completely visible and easily readable at small game size.

name: audio1010_ice_prompt
prompt: Create a production Neo Geo HD pixel-art sprite sheet for Bullets of Fury, 16-frame ICE LASER animation, strict 4 columns by 4 rows equal cells. Each cell is 128 pixels wide and 512 pixels tall conceptually; tall straight vertical beam, anchored exactly at same bottom muzzle point and fixed silhouette/width in every cell, firing NORTH. Rich cobalt/cyan crystalline ice laser with bright almost-white core, dark-blue pixel outlines, glittering needle ice crystals and frosted jagged side edges, crisp 16-bit pixel shading, genuinely ice not generic cyan electricity. Frames 1-4 show icy energy gathering and initial column forming; frames 5-12 held full-length beam with frozen particles/pulses advancing upward; frames 13-16 release with brittle ice fracture and separate shards. Same bottom source anchor, no panning/no whole beam rotation/no zoom. Real transparency between and around all cells. No backgrounds, no letters/numbers/gridlines. Cells never touch or bleed, strong crisp alpha edges, arcade authored pixels without soft halos. Include proper fully drawn muzzle crown at bottom; preserve same exact position across every frame. Exactly sixteen sequential distinct frames readable row-major.

name: audio1010_wind_prompt
prompt: Production sprite sheet for Bullets of Fury, Neo Geo HD pixel-art WIND weapon effects. EXACTLY sixteen equal sprite cells in a 4 by 4 grid, fixed conceptual 256 by 256 even square canvas in every cell. Rich emerald, turquoise and pale silver airflow, dark teal sharp pixel edges and richly shaded ribbons with small leaves and cut metal dust. Frames 1-4: bright small gust muzzle plume firing straight NORTH from same exact bottom-centre mount point, energy grows but source stays locked. Frames 5-8: elongated projectile spinning wind helix, northward motion implied by streaming particles but fixed mid-cell position. Frames 9-12: a compact tornado sphere swirling aggressively, true drawn twist perspective and loose sharp dust/debris, exactly same central pivot and common size each frame. Frames 13-16: impact wind-pressure explosion expanding into broken twisting crescent gusts and dissipating fine dust in last frame. Each four-frame section is an authored sub-bank, distinct sequential smooth frames. No labels, numbers, icons, grid, background, glow rectangles or cell overlap. Real alpha transparency, no soft halos. Crisp pixel shading, arcade-quality energy art, keep WIND recognizably wind rather than generic green fire or poison. Clear common pivots and cell margins, no per-frame zoom or translating whole effect.
